units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 1:1:17">Y. Taan. I, 64ᵃ</cite> top (expl.

<cite ref="Isaiah 21:11">Is. XXI, 11</cite>) <he>מה מילל ש׳ העולמים</he> what did the keeper of the world say? <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 36:2">Lev. R. s. 36</cite> <he>מה גפן זו הש׳ שלה עומד למעלה וֹכ׳</he> as the guard of the grape vine (vineyard) stands high (in the <cite ref="U00457"><he>שׁוֹמֵרָה</he></cite>), so is Israel’s guard above.
Ḥag. 15ᵇ אפי׳ ש׳ הפתח וכ׳ even the gate-keeper (of Gehenna) could not stand before thee; a. fr.—Esp. one in whose charge an object is given, bailee, ש׳ חנם an unpaid bailee; ש׳ שכר a paid trustee.
B. Mets. 93ᵇ; a. fr.—[Shebu. VIII, 1; B. Mets. VII, 8 נושא שכר, sub. שומר].—Trnsf. that part of a plant or of a body which serves as a protection (e.g. leaves, skin).
<cite ref="Berakhot 36b:4">Ber. 36ᵇ</cite> <he>היכא אמרינן דנעשה ש׳ לפירי וכ׳</he> we call a part of a plant a guard of the fruit only, if the plant dies when the guard is removed.

<cite ref="Chullin 119b:26">Ḥull. 119ᵇ</cite> <he>בשדרה משום ש׳</he> it refers to the stem of an ear, and because it is ‘a guard’; a. fr.—Pl. <he>שׁוֹמְרִים</he>, <he>שׁוֹמְרִין</he>. B. Mets. l. c. <he>שׁוֹמְרֵי פירות וכ׳</he> watchmen of fruits may eat (of them) by local usage, but not by Biblical law. Ib.; Shebu. l. c. <he>ארבעה ש׳ הן וכ׳</he> these are four classes of bailees. Ib. 49ᵇ <he>שבועת ש׳</he> the oath required of bailees (<cite ref="Exodus 22:9">Ex. XXII, 9</cite> sq.); a. fr.
